correctness.rationale: On the common additive lattice the quandle product is α(u)β(v), with α,β induced by multiplication by −1 and 2 on V. Both maps are automorphisms for odd p, preserving every I^r. Hence the span of I^r⋆I^s is exactly I^(r+s), and induction gives the same powers for every parenthesization. Writing t_i=e_(v_i)−1, the integral binomial relation first gives p t_i∈I² and then, by iterating p t_i=−t_i^p−p t_i(u_i−1), gives p t_i∈I^p and p t_i≡−t_i^p mod I^(p+1). Thus p kills positive graded layers and multiplication by t_j gives the claimed homogeneous relations. Conversely each nonzero character into Z[ζ_p] gives degree-r evaluation by dividing by (ζ_p−1)^r then reducing modulo ζ_p−1, whose residue ring is F_p. For a monomial its last nonzero index i is unchanged by reducing earlier exponents via X_j^p X_i=X_j X_i^p until they are <p. Successive last-index strata on projective points identify independent reduced polynomial functions on F_p^(i−1), proving injectivity and the vanishing ideal assertion. Counting these monomials verifies the series and sharp stabilization, including rank one. Degree-one action of α and β is by −1 and 2, respectively, so the twist is exactly (−1)^r2^s on degrees r,s. The frozen Smith/Hermite and evaluation checks were inspected, not executed; they are bounded corroboration, with the binary example a group-ring check only.
residual_risks: In the proof the surjection to the positive-degree algebra is understood on (P/J)_{>0}; the Finding states this correctly. The core result does not cover p=2.

evidence: Zhang gives Φ(Δ^n)=I L_((1−φ)G)^(n−1), with agreement of parenthesizations; φ=−1 gives I^n. The older accessible abstracts supply additive bases or presentations, and Chang–Tang explicitly determines successive quotients for all finite abelian G.
Tahara–Yamada report the earlier stabilization degree 3p−2 and stable rank p³+p²+p+1 for the elementary abelian group of rank four; that is the same specialization as here.

originality.rationale: The supported distinct claim is the positive-degree integral core-quandle graded-algebra identification by normalized cyclotomic evaluations with the projective point coordinate algebra and the explicit degree twist. The projective point ideal, transport of the filtration, and prior determination of additive augmentation quotients themselves are not new. The inspected material does not establish prior coverage of the combined identification. There is substantial residual risk of a direct antecedent for the ordinary graded ring or a basis that makes its presentation immediate.
residual_risks: Hales (1985) on the graded ring, Passi (1968) Theorem 4.7, and the detailed older augmentation bases or relations can affect priority; they were not available for full statement-level comparison. No claim of novelty is made for the projective ideal, the augmentation transport, or the additive determination in itself.

value.rationale: The character evaluation identifies multiplication between all graded layers in geometric coordinates, not just the layer sizes. It describes a natural filtration of a nonassociative ring and gives a usable all-degree multiplication model with an explicit twist. The value is in this structure, not in recomputing an additive order or establishing the already known point ideal.
residual_risks: A previously known equivalent ordinary graded presentation would materially reduce the incremental contribution; the result does not cover general exponent or Alexander action.
